status_summary: On 2025-12-04 the USPTO Director issued a memorandum to the examining corps on subject matter eligibility declarations and a companion memorandum to applicants on best practices for filing them; the corps memorandum says it creates no new practice. On 2025-12-05 the Deputy Commissioner for Patents issued an advance notice revising MPEP sections 2106.04 and 2106.05 to incorporate the precedential Ex Parte Desjardins decision, effective on issuance. The Patent Eligibility Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3152), which would rewrite Section 101, was introduced on 2025-05-01 and referred to the House Judiciary Committee. The statutory text of Section 101 is unchanged.

timeline.event: The Patent Eligibility Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3152) was introduced in the House and referred to the Judiciary Committee; it would rewrite Section 101 with a list of exclusions.

The USPTO Director issued a memorandum to the patent examining corps on subject matter eligibility declarations under Rule 132, and a companion memorandum to applicants and practitioners on best practices for submitting them.
The Deputy Commissioner for Patents issued an advance notice of changes to MPEP sections 2106.04 and 2106.05 incorporating the precedential Ex Parte Desjardins decision, effective on issuance.

title: Re-examine Section 101 patent eligibility for emerging technologies
uncertainties: The corps memorandum states that it does not create new practice, so its weight as reform is limited; the MPEP revision is the operative change. A Senate companion bill appeared in search results but was not opened, and the House bill's later status was not checked. The Mandate also asks for a balanced approach to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; the USPTO published proposed rules on Board practice on 2025-10-17 (Federal Register), which this record does not assess. Other 2025 eligibility guidance, such as any earlier memoranda on artificial intelligence claims, was not reviewed.
